messages.subject: "xy coordinates not in polygon" when using multiple polygons
messages.subject_clean: "xy coordinates not in polygon" when using multiple polygons
messages.body_plain:
I am getting an unexpected error ("xy coordinates not in polygon") when I try to use multiple polygons in secr.
In my (simulated) data, I searched several polygons within a larger area of interest, but I get the above error. I do not get an error if I search only one polygon, or if I search multiple trap grids.
My question is, does anyone recognize this issue or know a solution? Code and more comments below. I am using secr v. 2.10.2 and R v. 3.2.5.

# create area of interest
     poly.AV <- make.poly(x=c(0,0,14000,14000), y=c(0,14000,14000,0), exclusive=F)
# sim pop. buffer = zero because area is a habitat island
     my.pop <- sim.popn (D=0.0055, core=poly.AV, buffer = 0, model2D = "poisson", buffertype = "convex", Ndist = "poisson")
     plot(my.pop)

# several steps to create 35 small polygons to survey
     single.poly <- make.poly(x=c(0,0,1400,1400), y=c(0,1400,1400,0), exclusive=F)               # sample unit is 1% of total
     frame3 <- seq(from=560, by=1400, length=10)
     frame4 <- expand.grid(x=frame3, y=frame3)
     set.seed(128)  # 128 includes bottom left, only some "not in polygon". Seed 127 excludes bottom left and all "not in polygon"
     AV.trap.poly <- trap.builder(n = 35, cluster=single.poly, frame = frame4, method ="SRS", edgemethod = "allowoverlap",
                        samplefactor = 2, detector='polygon', plt = T, add =T)

# sim capthist
     capthist.AV.poly <- sim.capthist(traps=AV.trap.poly, popn=my.pop, detectpar=list(g0=0.5, sigma=350), noccasions=3)
     par(mar=c(1,2,3,2))
     plot(capthist.AV.poly, tracks = TRUE, varycol = T, lab1cap = T, laboffset = 15, title =
         paste("Simulated 'polygon' data", "D = 0.0055, g0 = 0.2, sigma = 350, nocc=3"))

# mask
     mask.AV <- make.mask(traps=poly.AV, buffer = 0, spacing = NULL, nx = 64, ny = 64, type ="traprect")  # seems correct

# fit model. yields error
     model3 <- secr.fit (capthist.AV.poly, model = list(D~1, g0~1, sigma~1), mask=mask.AV, buffer=0)

Various notes: If I use single.poly instead of AV.trap.poly in sim.capthist (and increase pop density or size of single.poly), it works. If I use cluster=make.grid in trap.builder, it works.
I tried make.poly(polylist) instead of trap.builder (not shown), and I got the same error.
I noticed that if AV.trap.poly includes the lower left corner, (set.seed(128)), the error applies to most, but not all detections. If the lower left is not included (set.seed(127)), the error applies to all detections.
Also, when I set frame3 from=700, which seems logical to me, AV.trap.poly does not line up with poly.AV. For some reason, from=560 lines up the two polygons. With make.poly(polylist), then from=0 lines up the polygons.
Can anyone help? Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: "xy coordinates not in polygon" when using multiple polygons
messages.subject_clean: "xy coordinates not in polygon" when using multiple polygons
messages.body_plain:
The immediate problem is in verify.capthist called by secr.fit, and can be suppressed by setting verify = FALSE in the call to secr.fit (which by the way doesn't use buffer=0 because you define a mask directly). That at least sets secr.fit going (slowly). The issue has to do with labelling (numbering) of polygons in the capthist object; I need to check whether it also affects secr.fit. Will get back to you on this in the next day or so.
Murray

messages.subject: Re: "xy coordinates not in polygon" when using multiple polygons
messages.subject_clean: "xy coordinates not in polygon" when using multiple polygons
messages.body_plain:
After some more checking, I am fairly sure the problem is restricted to verify, and only arises for polygon or transect detectors with varying number of digits in the polyID (1-9 vs 10-35 in this case). I have fixed it for the next release by adding leading zeros in split.traps. For now it is simple to avoid it by setting verify=FALSE.
Murray

messages.subject: Conditional likelihood VS full likelihood
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I'm working on density estimation of a black bear population with hair snag genotyping and I wondering which type of likelihood is better to use  (CL= TRUE or CL=FALSE)? I'm not sure about when to use one method rather than the other.

Thank you!

Pascal

messages.subject: Re: Conditional likelihood VS full likelihood
messages.body_plain:
Hi Pascal,
The two methods give identical results in most cases. With the full likelihood, density is a parameter in the model, but with the conditional likelihood, density must be estimated as a derived parameter after fitting the model. It's faster to fit models with CL = TRUE. However...

If you want to model spatial variation in density, you need the full likelihood.
If you want to model continuous individual covariates, you need the conditional likelihood, but categorical individual covariates can be usually be handled as groups or sessions in full likelihood models.

Note that you can't compare AICc between models fitted using different likelihoods, so you'll want to make this decision early.

All the best,
Eric

Murray
